item.title: STAFF POST OPEN - Crosslink Proposal
item.content:encoded:
The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team.

Show Reasoning
Hide Reasoning

The following crosslink is being suggested based on SCP-567's similarity to other SCP's involving disproportionate punishment of criminals.

Editing this:

Each cell appears to have its own unique trigger conditions in order to activate, which seem to involve committing some sort of criminal or heretical act.

To this:

Each cell appears to have its own unique trigger conditions in order to activate, which seem to involve committing some sort of criminal or heretical act.1

Footnotes
1. These triggers and resulting responses are similar to other anomalies involving disproportionate law enforcement, such as SCP-1002 and SCP-2701.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Right from the containment procedures, two red flags are being raised:

1. How are you supposed to scientifically establish subjective concepts like "Be of moderate political beliefs", "Have strong convictions as to the importance of upholding the law" and "Have a strong fear of offending others with their actions"?
Hell, I very much doubt it's even possible to work for the SCP Foundation and "have a strong fear of offending others". It doesn't help that nothing in the description or incident report justifies these requirements.

2. Redactions in containment procedures. Don't do it. These procedures exist so the people reading the report knows how to contain the SCP. Redacting anything in that paragraph prevents them from doing the one thing the SCP Foundation was created to do and beats the purpose of having these reports in the first place.

In general, there are far too many redactions and expungements. It gets grating, loses the mysterious and disturbing aura that causes people to imagine things worse than anything the author could have written, makes you lose interest in what's behind them and just ends up making the reader wonder why the author is even bothering writing this if they're not going to describe anything.

On top of that, the attempts at being disturbing come off as trying too hard to me, not to mention I'm getting tired of the "victim rants about their experience yet never goes into specifics" cliché.

There is also no reason for the description of SCP-567-5's trigger to redirect to an addendum.

The incident report brings even more problems. Aside from the same problem with excessive redactions and expungements, it is rather confusing that the doors are stated to slam shut as Clef entered (by the way, hurray for yet another random unexplained "Clef is the devil" moment) when both the main article and the incident report itself seem to imply that the cells are normally closed, what with them opening to release instances of SCP-567-9 and the final entry in the report specifically mentioning the door closing after releasing an instance.

item.content:encoded:
First off, I think the premise of this SCP is awesome. It's sufficiently creepy and mysterious. However, I felt that redacted and expunged were overused. While it is true that omissions can add a certain fear of the unknown flavor to any story, it just felt lazy here. For example: in SCP-567-9-1, "Though it walked on four limbs, its front limbs had [REDACTED] capable of operating complex devices." the redaction is just frustrating, like it couldn't be decided if tentacles, fingers or claws were creepier, so a general "aw, f*** it" was given and a redacted was posted. I would really like to see this one given a more thorough work over, giving a more complete descriptions of creatures and events (shadowy and unclear is fine, completely obscured is boring), and saving the omissions for what happens.

That said, I still think it's worth an upvote. Overall good job, Severe.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The way I interpret it, they're prisoners drawn in by similar facilities in other locations/dimensions/etc., all of which lead to some common super-prison. When escaping, they take the first exit that presents itself, and sometimes that leads to SCP-567. As for why they're universally hostile and aggressive: They're "criminals" (term used loosely) that have been sucked into some sort of alien prison and tortured somehow - that kind of thing doesn't exactly do wonders for one's mental stability, nor does escaping into yet another alien world.

I've already corrected this in the SCP and the test log, but for future reference: "Foundation" should be capitalized when referring to the SCP Foundation.
